senses.definition: A period of time devoted to a particular activity.
examples: "Are we having a recording session?" / "Yes. We've even got some session musicians to provide some brass."

quotes.text: Alternatively, if the patient is stuck ritualizing before session, then the therapist might want to create contingencies that might help the patient come in on time

senses.definition: An official meeting or term of a council, court, or other body to conduct its business; e.g. the annual or semiannual periods of a legislature (that together comprise the legislative term), whose individual meetings are also called sessions.
examples: This court is now in session.

senses.definition: (computing) The sequence of interactions between client and server, or between user and system; the period during which a user is logged in or connected.
examples: Logging out or shutting down the computer will end your session.

senses.definition: (cricket) Any of the three scheduled two-hour playing sessions, from the start of play to lunch, from lunch to tea and from tea to the close of play.
(chiefly obsolete or theology) The act of sitting, or the state of being seated.

quotes.text: So much his ascension into heaven and his session at the right hand of God do import.

senses.definition: (music) Ellipsis of jam session, used in isolate particularly for folk music.
(education) An academic term; semester; school year.
(beer) An extended period of drinking, typically consuming beer with low alcohol content.
(Presbyterianism) The ruling body of a congregation, consisting of the pastor and elders.
(music) To hold or participate in a jam session with other musicians.
